That defendant No. 1-3/5/8 contested the suit by filing a written statement contending inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable in its form, the same was barred by limitation and defect of parties. The substantive case of these defendants, ire shrot, was that the owner of the scheduled property was Dada Pramanik, who died laving son Kalimuddin and daughter Sundori Khatun. C.S. khatin No. 11 was wrongly prepared in the name of Kalimuddin only, Kalimuddin died leaving wife Kachhiron, son Nurul fioqud Paramanik and daughter Bahaton Nessa. Sundori Khatun died leaving two sons Bazitullah, Abdul Zabbar and two daugh-ters Nloyjan and Toyjan. Nurul Hoque died leaving mother Kachiron and wife Rashida Khatun. Ghatu Pramanik was not the brother of Dada Pramanik. Moslem was not the cousin of Nurul Islam. Bahatan Nessa died leaving son Sharnsad, who died leaving behind wife Sedan Khatun, two sons Nabir, Kabir, three daughters Nurjahan, Nur Mahal and Nir Baru. Shamsad transferred .70 acre of land to Kachiron by registered deed No. 6662 dated 06.11.1961. S.A. khatian No. 14 was wrongly prepared in the name of Abdul Zabbar and others without including the name of Kachhiron. Nurul Hoque was entitled to get 1.271/4 acres of land in C.S. Khatian No.11. He sold .4050 acre of land to Korban Ali. Azhar Ali and Haider Ali by various deeds. Nurul Hoque transferred .31 acre of land from1Khai schedule in C.S. khatian No. 42, plot No. 209. He transferred 1.31 acres to Rashida Begum (defendant No.1) by registred Heba-Bil-Ewaj deed dated 22.07.1969. Kachiron nessa transferred 1.03 acres of land from 'Ka' schedule and .31 acre from 'Kha' scheduled total 1.34 acres to defendants No.2 and 3 by registered heba deed dated 25.03.1992. Abdul Zabbar died leaving two sons Md. Abu Taleb, Md. Mohammad Ali and six daughters Soneka, Nobia Nessa, Zahura, Sara and Shahana. 'Kha' scheduled land originally belonged to Zan Mohammad. The heirs of Zan Mohammad soled .36 acre of land of Kachhiron nessa by various deed who transferred the same to defendants No.2 and 3 on 25.03.1992. Rasuldi Paranaki was the owner of 'Ga' scheduled land. The plaintiffs did not make any explanation regarding 1.60 acres of land described in schedule 'Ga' to the plaint. The plaintiffs did not bring the whole property into common hotch pot. The suit is bad for defect if parties. The suit should be dismissed. 

 6. Mr. Ali Tmam Khaled Rahim, learned Advocate appearing for the contesting defendant respondents, in his submission states that since the instant suit is a suit for partition and respective khatians had not been produced in the Court of facts for bringing all the lands of disputed jamas in hotch pot, the High Court Division rightly remanded the case to dispose of the matter giving opportunity to the parties to pro-duce khatians. 

 7. It appears from the materials on record that the instant suit for partition was instituted in respect of the land regarding in C.S. khatians No. 11, 69, 42, 13, 601, 14, 17 and 572 as described in the schedule "Ka', Kha' and 'Ga' to the plaint. It further appears that respective C.S. khatians as well as S.A. khatians were not produced in the Courts below and that the defendants produced 15 registered deeds and series of rent receipts in supported of their claim but the Courts below did not consider those documents. The High Court Division remanded the suit for hearing afresh giving the parties opportunity to produce of those relevant khatians. It is well settled that the appellate Court has the authority to consider the case after recording additional evidence if those are found to be required for proper adjudication of the matter in dispute upon fulfilling the provisions provided in Order LXI Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
